correctness.rationale: The exact cycle independent-set count and pair counts were independently reconstructed by occupancy gap compositions and verified against brute-force enumeration for n<=15. A configuration-swap lemma proves that only the constant mode is null at all n>=2k+1. Uniform weak compositions of a fixed excess m converge to m uniform ordered defect positions; Fourier moment convergence gives the telegraph-correlation kernel (1-2t)^m. At most m vacant-vacant bonds supply O_m((1+|r|)^-2) tail control, proving ell-one convergence, its 1/4 sum rule and parity-sensitive asymptotics. The packaged standalone Python checker passed 1678 assertions; finite tests are corroboration, not proof of the limiting theorem.

originality.rationale: Previously reviewed mathematical claims and published research-record near matches were compared by distributions, quantifiers and limiting regimes. Full text of Davies–Perkins and relevant parts of Bakhti–Müller–Maass were materially inspected. Algorithmic canonical sampling, a fixed-distance pair covariance, grand-canonical Fibonacci covariance, and Poisson-defect length-three spectra do not state or imply the fixed-m canonical length-two ell-one Bragg Fourier theorem. Priority risk remains for a differently named conditioned telegraph or lattice-gas structure factor; novelty is provisional, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Fixed-jump random-telegraph diffraction may have appeared under scattering or renewal terminology not indexed by the searches.
The broad 2013 hard-rod correlations may yield finite formula specializations; inspected text does not prove none can, and historical priority is not independently certified.
Indexed published-finding corpus records were not all inspected at primary full text; this limits exhaustive priority claims.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical fixed-size near-maximal cycle independent-set ensemble, and its natural invariant is the entire covariance Fourier intensity spectrum. The result goes beyond finite enumerations: ell-one convergence captures all spectral mass on the O(1) Bragg-index scale, exhibits an even/odd phase-slip distinction, supplies sharp 1/r^2 tail and explicit one- and two-defect closed forms, and gives an exact finite injectivity boundary. This clarifies near-crystalline harmonic observability, not arbitrary small numerical parameter gains.
